summary: Redwood AE/SE demo of Redwood Console + Optimize focusing on evaluation workflows: prompt sets, automated regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Customer concerned about data residency, KMS, and latency for point-of-care use. Agreed next steps: share sample eval artifacts, pilot with 200 prompts, and send pricing/deployment options.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Maya, Carlos, Ethan, Lina — thanks for making time. We wanted to walk you through Redwood's evaluation and quality monitoring flow in the Console and Optimize, focusing on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Quick intros, Priya is our SE who will do most of the demo.
[00:18] Maya (AtlasHealth): Hey Jordan, thanks. Quick context — we run clinical triage suggestions inside our patient portal, latency target 300ms 95th, and strict PHI rules. We're exploring hosted vs private.
[00:35] Jordan: Got it — we'll call out the Dedicated and Private options. Priya, want to kick off?
[00:40] Priya (Redwood SE): Sure. I'm going to share my screen. First slide — eval pipeline in Redwood Optimize: you can define prompt sets, label outputs, attach metrics, and then configure regression alerts on those metrics. Example: accuracy, hallucination rate, ROUGE-like overlap, or custom scoring.
[01:05] Carlos (AtlasHealth): When you say "prompt sets" are those tied to routes in the API or just generic collections?
[01:12] Priya: Good question. They can be both. You can bind a prompt set to a route or keep it workspace-level. For the pilot we'd usually map your production route for triage -> a prompt set that mirrors real traffic.
[01:30] Ethan: Do we need to reformat prompts for the Console? We have JSON records with context.
[01:37] Priya: You can ingest JSONL. The Console accepts a schema mapping (context, question, expected_answer). We have examples. We'll share the sample template after.
[01:50] Jordan: A couple of quick clarifications on security — for PHI you mentioned private deployments?
[01:56] Maya: Yes, we prefer Private or Dedicated with VPC and customer-managed KMS. SOC 2 is a must.
[02:04] Priya: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations and VPC peering. We also emit audit logs per request and offer retention controls. We're SOC 2 Type II-compliant; we'll send the security pack.
[02:20] Carlos: Good. On latency — if we use dedicated nodes, predictable 95th targets look realistic?
[02:26] Jordan: Dedicated is what most folks use for predictable p95. We can surface per-route token-level latency in the Console.
[02:34] Priya: Switching to the Console demo — here is the Eval dashboard. Top panel: overall pass rate, drift over time. Below: prompt set table with tags (triage, policy, edge-cases).
[02:50] Jordan: Note the ability to tag prompts for cohorts — e.g., 'age>65', 'cardio-related', 'rare-conditions' — helps slice metrics.
[03:04] Maya: Can you demo regression alerts?
[03:08] Priya: Sure. Click into a prompt set, go to Alerts. You can create a regression alert where you pick metric (e.g., exact match rate), baseline range, sensitivity, and alert channels (Slack, webhook, email). We show a sample alert that triggers when pass rate drops by 6% sustained over 24 hours.
[03:28] Ethan: Is the baseline anchored to a pinned model/version? How do A/B tests factor in?
[03:33] Priya: Baseline is typically a pinned model version. For A/B you can create a controlled rollout and compare cohorts: control uses model v1, candidate v2. The Eval dashboard will show side-by-side metrics and highlight statistically significant regressions.
[03:52] Jordan: We also have automatic cohort detection — if certain prompts start failing by user segment, the system suggests cohort slices to monitor.
[04:03] Lina: Does the regression alert pipeline re-run with updated labels if we backfill?
[04:09] Priya: Yes — you can re-run evaluations on historic data. If you update labels, we re-evaluate and the dashboard reflects the updated pass rates.
[04:20] Carlos: How are labels handled — manual or ML-assisted?
[04:24] Priya: Both. You can do manual human-in-the-loop labeling in the Console, or you can upload labels via CSV/JSONL. We also provide weak-labeling suggestions using heuristics to speed up labeling.
[04:38] Jordan: Let's demo an A/B comparison quickly — I'll switch to the A/B tab. Here we have two cohorts, 1k prompts each; candidate shows slight drop in exact match but better BLEU/semantic score.
[04:58] Priya: You'll see the confidence intervals and p-values. The dashboard flags whether differences are statistically significant given sample size. If not significant, you can increase sample size or run stratified analysis.
[05:15] Maya: For our safety team, we'd need to see explainability — per-token attention or why an output was flagged. Is that available?
[05:22] Priya: We surface model outputs, diff between models, and an annotation timeline. We don't expose raw attention for every model yet, but we provide token-level score breakdowns and a 'why this failed' rationale from the eval rules engine.
[05:38] Carlos: About alerts — can they trigger automated rollbacks in Dedicated/Private?
[05:44] Jordan: You can hook alerts to the rollout policy. For Dedicated we support automatic fallback to a pinned stable variant if critical alerts fire. For Private deployments, we can expose the same control plane; automatic rollback depends on customer's change control — usually we wire webhooks so your infra can decide.
[06:05] Ethan: What's the overhead of routing traffic for A/B? Any added latency?
[06:10] Priya: Negligible for batching-enabled routes — we sample traffic at the edge, send to both variants depending on routing policy. For synchronous latency-sensitive paths, we recommend shadowing (async) or a small sample for direct A/B. We'll show sample configs.
[06:28] Jordan: Turning to prompt sets — here's a prompt set for triage. Notice fields: id, prompt_text, expected_answer, tags, cohort. You can enrich with metadata like patient_age_range.
[06:43] Maya: Could we import directly from our analytics DB? We have an API export.
[06:47] Priya: Yes, the Console supports scheduled imports from S3/Blob or direct API ingestion via JSONL. We can also connect to your data pipeline; we'll show a template.
[06:58] Jordan: Now regression alerts on an example metric — hallucination rate measured by a regex-based detector + manual review signal.
[07:08] Priya: The demo shows an alert fired last week for a cohort 'cardio-urgent' — drill-in shows 18% hallucination increase vs baseline. The alert shows example failing prompts and candidate outputs so you can triage quickly.
[07:26] Carlos: How are false positives managed? We can't have noisy alerts.
[07:30] Priya: You tune sensitivity, minimum sample size, and use rolling windows. You can also add human-in-the-loop thresholds — e.g., only escalate after triage channel confirms.
[07:44] Ethan: A/B: can we run cost-per-inference comparisons side-by-side to pick cheaper variant if quality similar?
[07:50] Priya: Yes, the Optimize dashboard has cost per token and cost per successful inference metrics and you can surface cost/quality tradeoffs.
[07:59] Jordan: Let's show how to annotate and push labels back for model fine-tuning or for the eval baseline. Priya: here we annotate five failing examples, then export as CSV or push to an S3 bucket for training.
[08:18] Maya: Do you integrate with our MLOps workflow? We use Airflow/Kubernetes.
[08:22] Priya: We have a REST API and webhooks; many customers wire exports to S3 and have Airflow ingest them. For Dedicated/Private we can provide a connector that writes artifacts directly to your internal storage.
[08:36] Jordan: Switching focus — technical deep dive: how regression detection works under the hood. Priya?
[08:40] Priya: We compute per-prompt metrics and aggregate by cohort. We use bootstrapped confidence intervals and controls for multiple comparisons. Alerts are triggered based on user-selected alpha and effect size. There's also an option for delta-testing and Thompson sampling for A/B.
[09:02] Carlos: Any gotchas with small sample sizes?
[09:05] Priya: With n<100 you get wide intervals; the dashboard will show that and recommend larger sample sizes. We also support sequential testing with alpha spend controls.
[09:17] Maya: For our compliance team, we need exports of eval results for audits. Is that supported?
[09:22] Priya: Yes — you can export time-series of metrics, raw examples, and audit logs. Exports can be stored in your S3 or delivered via secure link.
[09:33] Jordan: Quick note on model variants: Redwood Verified models include performance profiles; you can also bring-your-own model. For private we support on-prem models behind your network.
[09:45] Ethan: About bring-your-own model — if we host inside our VPC, can the Console still ingest eval metrics?
[09:51] Priya: Yes — we have a private data plane option that forwards metrics to your storage and the control plane shows aggregated dashboards. For full air-gapped setups, we offer a self-hosted console package.
[10:05] Maya: Let's talk about sample sizes for the pilot. We said 200 prompts earlier — is that enough?
[10:10] Priya: For coarse signals, 200 could show big regressions but might not catch small deltas. For statistical A/B you'd want 1k+ per cohort. For initial pilot 200 is fine to sanity-check quality and integration.
[10:23] Jordan: Real quick, walk-through of an alert email — it shows metric, baseline, current, top failing examples, and a link to the Console with pre-filtered view.
[10:36] Priya: I'll show an example Slack alert — includes a quick summary and a link. There's also a webhook payload you can parse to trigger your runbook automation.
[10:47] Carlos: Any chance we can run a smoke benchmark on our RDS-hosted dataset? We want to test p95 under load.
[10:53] Jordan: Absolutely — part of the pilot we can schedule a bench run against a snapshot. We'll coordinate with your infra.
[11:01] Maya: About cost — what does the pilot cost look like?
[11:05] Jordan: For pilot we often provide a small hosted credit (depends on scale) and charge primarily for bench runs + Dedicated setup if requested. I'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[11:17] Priya: Back to Console features — here's the A/B comparison UI showing side-by-side distributions, per-cohort alerts, and the ability to drill into individual examples and add labels.
[11:34] Ethan: Can we export diffs for downstream analytics?
[11:37] Priya: Yes, diffs export as JSONL or CSV with metadata tags.
[11:44] Jordan: A quick demo of labeling workflow — we assign 3 reviewers, label 50 examples, consensus step runs, and results propagate.
[11:58] Maya: How do you handle PII/PHI in exported examples? We need redaction.
[12:04] Priya: We support automatic redaction filters at ingestion and you can configure sensitive field masking. For Private deployments you can keep raw examples internal and only export hashed artifacts.
[12:20] Carlos: On the infra side, do you support customer-managed keys?
[12:24] Priya: Yes, KMS/HSM integration for Private and Dedicated. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
[12:33] Jordan: Now a short walkthrough of regression alert tuning — you can make alerts more specific by combining metric conditions and cohort filters.
[12:46] Priya: For example, require min sample 50 and aggregate over 24h with a 5% effect size.
[12:55] Ethan: One more question — can we tie alerts to PRs in our repo or ticketing?
[12:59] Priya: Yes, webhooks can create JIRA tickets or GitHub issues; we also have an integration for PagerDuty.
[13:12] Maya: Ok this is helpful. For next steps, we need the security docs and a sample prompt set.
[13:18] Jordan: We'll send those. Priya, anything else to demo?
[13:20] Priya: I'll demo a quick drift detection example — here we have lexical drift and semantic drift graphs. When semantic similarity drops for a cohort we mark it.
[13:34] Carlos: How is semantic similarity computed?
[13:36] Priya: Using embeddings with a configurable similarity threshold; you can pick your embedding model.
[13:42] Maya: For our compliance we need retention controls on both inputs and outputs.
[13:46] Priya: We support configurable retention per workspace and data classification tags. You can set auto-delete policies.
[13:56] Jordan: Time check — 16 minutes in, want to recap?
[14:00] Maya: Yes. High-level — we like the eval workflow and alerting. Questions: pilot scope (200 prompts), security pack, bench run.
[14:09] Jordan: Great. We'll capture actions. Priya, any final pointers?
[14:13] Priya: Just that for the pilot we'll recommend a small A/B or shadow run, ingest your 200 prompts, set up 2 regression alerts, and run a bench. We'll provide the eval template.
[14:26] Ethan: For the bench, can we test with our Dockerized model as candidate behind our VPC?
[14:31] Priya: Yes, we can coordinate. For private we usually set up a data plane connector and run bench traffic through it.
[14:40] Carlos: On the data plane connector — what's the network model?
[14:43] Priya: VPC peering or private link depending on cloud. For on-prem we support a VPN tunnel or an agent. We'll share the topology diagram.
[14:55] Maya: After the pilot, assuming metrics hold, we'll look at Dedicated vs Private pricing.
[15:01] Jordan: Sounds good. Any other competitor concerns?
[15:05] Maya: We evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI — main differences are in cost and managed safety features. We want the auditability.
[15:13] Jordan: We'll include a feature comparison.
[15:16] Priya: Final quick note: you can automate remediation runbooks from alerts so triage is quick.
[15:25] Jordan: Ok wrapping up — we'll send the security pack, sample eval template, and pricing. Pilot next steps noted. Thanks all.
[15:34] Maya: Thanks Jordan, Priya.
[15:36] Ethan: Thanks.
[15:38] Carlos: Bye.

[End of transcript — recording 45:02 (approx). Notes: transcription has minor errors and speaker overlaps occasionally.]
